reviewDisciplineNote: One candidate finding was available and I declined it deliberately. basedOn.g01v1.role still reads 'exactByteIntent is quoted' without mentioning that passProperty is now quoted too. I did not charge it, for two reasons. First, it is true and makes no exclusivity claim — it describes what the pin supplies, not an exhaustive source list — and every field that does make a source attribution now names both. Second, that field was present and unchanged in v1, I saw it, and I did not charge it then; the finding I wrote was scoped to the three attributing fields. Escalating to an adjacent field after the author landed exactly the fix I specified would move the goalposts and make the review cycle non-convergent. If I had wanted that sentence widened, the place to say so was the v1 verdict.
observationsNotFindings: The fold is unusually disciplined for a wording correction. The temptation in landing an attribution finding is to also tidy the catalog while the file is open; instead initialStates is byte-identical to v1 and the only structural addition is the findingDisposition record. That makes the change auditable in a single comparison, which is what let me refute the over-broad-fold attack by measurement rather than by argument.

The 'Per platform:' prefix in exactByteIntent still grammatically introduces all seven items while the subject expands only the first two per platform. I did not charge this in v1 and do not charge it now; the reasoning is unchanged. At least one listed item, the D-006 numeral 25 MB, is manifestly a single threshold constant and cannot be per-platform, so the prefix demonstrably does not distribute over the whole list, the subject makes no exhaustiveness claim, and the pinned source remains available to a later fixture cycle. It is recorded here only so the ambiguity stays visible in the chain.

The chain remains single-reviewer end to end. No Codex artifact exists for g01-input-corpus v1 or v2, nor for G01 harness v1, v2 or v3. That is the standing worth carrying forward rather than a defect in this artifact.

The D-006 handling survives the fold intact, including the four per-platform repetitions of the double denial. A fold that rewrites attribution prose is exactly where such repeated denials tend to get collapsed into one; they were not.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. CLAUDE-G01IC-V1-SF1 is landed in all three locations I charged, and I verified it structurally rather than by reading the prose: splitting whatIsAuthored on 'passProperty:' and searching the leading segment for 'defaultInstall' returns absent, and the newly declared split of twelve exactByteIntent states to one passProperty state matches a recount of the array exactly. The two attacks that mattered on a fold both fail. It is not cosmetic — no top-level field still attributes the exclusion state to exactByteIntent, and the attribution now matches the harness bytes, where 'defaultInstall' occurs in passProperty and not in exactByteIntent. It is not over-broad — initialStates is byte-identical to frozen v1 by ==, as are assertsNamedNotAuthored, whatIsNotAuthored and doesNot, with findingDisposition the only added key, so its claim that no named state was added or removed is true on the bytes. All five cited digests recompute, including the two new predecessor pins, and the characterisation of my own v1 verdict as 'REJECT 0/1' matches the frozen file field for field. Every prohibition holds: MiB, mebibyte, megabyte, 1048576 and 1024 all return zero, all nine occurrences of 26214400 are negations read individually, SATISFIED and QUALIFIED occur zero times, and the only DR-G token is the already-named DR-G01. One candidate finding on basedOn.g01v1.role was available and I declined it on the record, because that field was unchanged from v1 and I did not charge it then. 18 attacks run, 18 refuted.
